newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: New Congo sees bright future for copper industry.
newsitem.headline: New Congo sees bright future for copper industry.

text.p: The Democratic Republic of Congo expects demand for its main export earner, copper, to increase in the short to medium term, Mines Minister Florent Mututulo said.
Mututulo told delegates to a sub-Saharan Oil and Minerals conference on Tuesday night that demand for copper out of Asia augured well for the country's mining industry.
"Most analysts predict a price in the range of $1.25 to $1.30 a pound in the short to medium term.
"This is from the huge increase in demand from the Asian countries...This augers well for the future of our country," Mututulo said.
He said although the country held vast reserves of copper and cobalt, among the largest in the world, lack of investment had prevented exploration.

"The potential for discovering millions of tonnes of new reserves is prevented only by the investment required for exploration and the willingness and determination of the foreign partners we hope to attract," Mututulo said.
He said the potential for new copper discoveries stretched beyond the traditional copper province of Katanga, formerly Shaba.
Mututulo said the country also intended to increase output of gold in a mining sector regarded by the former government as its private domain.
He said the Congo would launch serious economic reforms soon, including reviewing the country's mining and investment codes.
"A serious reform will be undertaken in the very near future in order to (make) the following more adaptable in the modern investment climate, the investment code, the mining code and the fiscal."
He said the Congo was keen to do business but would not allow monopolies. "Monopoly is a word that is banned in my country."
Existing contracts with foreign companies would be studied and, if necessary, renegotiated.
"All contracts...need to be scrutinised and in some cases renegotiated in the light of our government's policy of fair and equitable deals."
Mututulo said the state of the country's economy was alarming and that drastic action was required.
Mining analysts see the former Zaire as one of the richest unexplored mining resource regions in the world with vast untapped resources of copper, cobalt, diamonds and gold.
Mututulo said the country was devastated under the regime of Mobutu Sese Seko, and he accused Mobuto's officials of rampant corruption.
"Fraud became synonymous with management...You cannot mine copper in a fleet of Mercedes."
